clue.text: Exhibit pole reinforced with two metallic elements

indicators.note: a pole reinforced with something has it set into its core, so the elements go inside the pole

parts.note: a mast is a tall pole, as on a ship
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A display of a flagpole strengthened with a couple of metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhibit' looks like a noun but is a verb here; 'reinforced with' is the container signal, the two chemical symbols packing the pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit a feeling is to show it plainly, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Maureen got out of bed sour-tempered

parts.note: Mo is a common short form of the name Maureen
to get out of bed in the morning is to rise, past tense rose

explanation.surface: Maureen woke up grumpy and got out of bed in a foul mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose describes a gloomy, sullen person, one who is bad-tempered.

clue.text: Wise man buries gold under secluded place

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece written under another follows it

parts.note: a nest is a snug, secluded retreat
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A sage hides his treasure beneath a hidden refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buries' is only a link here, though it fits the scene; 'under' orders the pieces, as the clue is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, Nestor is the aged Greek king famed for wise counsel, so his name stands for any sage elder.

clue.text: Pollution over a big town brings instability

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, so before, the rest

parts.note: a fug is a stuffy, smoky, polluted atmosphere
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Smog hanging over a large town makes it an unsettled place.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugacity is fleetingness or transience, a lack of stability or permanence.

clue.text: Ask for guru perhaps to be heard

indicators.note: something to be heard is spoken aloud, so the word is chosen by its sound

parts.note: the gurus who founded Sikhism were Sikhs, so a guru may be one

explanation.surface: Ask a spiritual teacher for advice, maybe, so he can be listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek something is to request or try to obtain it.

clue.text: Did a jig, almost comic, going round the church

indicators.note: one piece going round another encloses it, so the church sits inside
almost means the last letter is lost

parts.note: The Dandy is a long-running British children's comic
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A clownish figure capered about the parish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the comic's final letter and 'going round' wraps the remainder about the church. The Dandy is a long-running British comic magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance a jig is simply to have danced, the jig being one lively folk step.

clue.text: Fire up a girl outside university

indicators.note: the girl stands outside, so wraps around, the university

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl waiting outside the university gets someone excited.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to stir or excite them.

clue.text: Commander of light brigade — buttoned-up type?

definitions.meaning: the Earl who led the Charge of the Light Brigade in the Crimean War
a knitted jacket that fastens with buttons down the front

explanation.surface: A dashing cavalry officer who is rather starchy and reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buttoned-up' suggests someone prim, but it is a garment literally buttoned up; the jacket was named after the Earl.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh Earl, cavalry leader at Balaclava, gave his title to the knitted woollen jacket with buttons.

clue.text: Insult makes Greek character blush, being upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to blush is to go red

explanation.surface: An insult causes a Greek person to flush with distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' turns the whole run ETA GORED backwards. 'makes' is a link. 'Greek character' means a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To derogate is to disparage or belittle, as an insult does.

clue.text: Agreed a new contact or stepped down?

definitions.meaning: put one's name again to a fresh deal
left a job or post voluntarily

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-signed it means signed again, a renewed deal; read whole it means quit one's post.

clue.text: Repugnance shown by bishop in house with soldiers

indicators.note: the bishop is placed in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: Disgust felt at a bishop sharing a house with troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror is intense fear or loathing, a strong feeling of revulsion.

clue.text: However, Anthony is like a pearly king

parts.note: but can mean however
Tony is the short form of Anthony

explanation.surface: Yet a man named Anthony resembles a costermonger in his finery.
explanation.walkthrough: A pearly king is a London street trader whose suit is covered with mother-of-pearl buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearly king's suit is studded with thousands of buttons, so he is covered in them.

clue.text: Pet's first bit of supper — sponge

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to sponge off someone is to mooch, cadge freebies

explanation.surface: A pet animal grabs the first scrap of dinner and goes scrounging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is a verb, to cuddle; the 's means 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet in the romantic sense is to kiss and cuddle, the same as this verb.

clue.text: In the audience ask heather: who is a traitor?

indicators.note: what the audience hears is spoken, so this phrase points to a sound

parts.note: to ask is to quiz, and ling is a name for heather

explanation.surface: A listener asks a woman called Heather who betrayed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, LING. Vidkun Quisling collaborated with the Nazis in Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a Norwegian Nazi collaborator, the word now means any collaborating betrayer.

clue.text: Back a role for each person wanting to acquire fur?

indicators.note: back means the word for role is read in reverse

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
per means for each, as in per head

explanation.surface: A theatrical role that each actor wants, playing a fur dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapper catches animals in traps to get their pelts.

clue.text: Repeat the thing time after time — to the end of time!

indicators.note: the first time follows the second time, so the second is placed first

parts.note: it can stand for a thing
an era is a span of time
an era is a span of time

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Say the same thing again and again, right till the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do something again, repeatedly.

clue.text: Such may be involved in acts

definitions.text: Such may be involved in acts

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Those taking part in the acts of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ACTS, and the troupe of actors are the people involved in acts of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is the group of actors in a play, who perform its acts.

clue.text: Female on trial wrecked old household item

indicators.note: wrecked means broken up, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A woman in court smashed an antique domestic object.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron was the heated metal tool once used to press clothes at home.

clue.text: A security device for the flight

definitions.text: A security device for the flight

parts.words: A security device for the flight
parts.note: the flight is a staircase, not an aircraft, and the device keeps climbers safe by giving a handrail

explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail on a staircase, keeping people safe on the stairs.

clue.text: A terrible anthem leads to a solemn ecclesiastical curse

indicators.note: terrible means very poorly made, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A badly sung hymn leads the church to pronounce a solemn curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is a formal excommunication pronounced by the church.

clue.text: Penny goes to the meadow in spring

parts.note: a lea is a meadow in poetry

explanation.surface: Penny walks out to the field in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' reads like the season but is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap is to jump or spring.

clue.text: Start work at nine, about? Good!

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so nine is read backwards

explanation.surface: Begin the job at around nine o'clock, excellent!
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'roughly' but turns NINE into ENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a beginning or start.

clue.text: One woman to quarrel with another

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
Ena is another woman's name

explanation.surface: One woman falls out with another.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowena is a woman's name, as in Scott's Ivanhoe.

clue.text: One learner among a number queuing up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the learner goes among the letters of the number

parts.note: nine is a number
L is the learner plate symbol

explanation.surface: A single learner driver among several waiting in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in line is to be waiting one behind another in a queue.

clue.text: Design that is evident in unkind person

parts.note: to design something is to intend or mean it
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A deliberate plan shows clearly in a nasty individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is an ungenerous or unkind person.

clue.text: Converted idolater's adapted

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An idol worshipper who changed faith has adjusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailored means made to fit or adjusted to suit a purpose.

clue.text: Position adopted by remotest ancestors

indicators.note: adopted by means taken into, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: The posture our most distant forebears took up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a stated position or attitude.

clue.text: Negative Tory's refusal of consent

indicators.note: 's stands for has, the words having the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP who votes no turns down a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is the right to reject a proposal, or its exercise.

clue.text: Pretty nasty little beast approaching the girl

parts.note: a rat is a disliked rodent
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A rather unpleasant creature creeping up on a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' is not attractive but an adverb, as in pretty good.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty and this adverb both mean fairly or somewhat.

clue.text: This sort of philosopher is explosive, then surprisingly genial

parts.note: HE is high explosive

indicators.note: surprisingly means in an unexpected way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A philosopher who blows up and then becomes oddly friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hegelian follows the German thinker Hegel's dialectical philosophy.

clue.text: Absence of path to cross river in the country

indicators.note: to cross means stretching across, so the path phrase goes around the river

parts.note: no way means there is no path

explanation.surface: No path crosses the river anywhere in this region.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian nation.

clue.text: Mark well a boy in school somersaulting

indicators.note: the boy and the a are placed inside the school
somersaulting turns the school name head over heels, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school
Ben is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A pupil tumbling about at a boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somersaulting' flips the school's name to give NOTE; 'in' then sets the article and the boy's name within it. Eton is an English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Nota bene is Latin for note well, the instruction to mark carefully.
